entries.title: Gen AI inside existing search engines overtakes standalone gen AI
entries.quote: In terms of daily use, accessing gen AI within a search engine (when a search yields a synthesis of results) will be 300% more common than using any standalone gen AI tool.
entries.metric: daily use of gen AI in search vs standalone tools
entries.subject: Generative AI adoption (embedded vs standalone)

entries.title: Why AI's next phase will likely demand more computational power, not less
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that "inference"—running AI models—will account for two-thirds of all AI computing power by 2026.
entries.metric: inference share of AI computing power
entries.subject: AI inference compute

entries.title: Unlocking exponential value with AI agent orchestration
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that if enterprises orchestrate agents better and thoughtfully address the associated challenges and risks, this market projection could increase by 15% to 30%—or as high as $45 billion by 2030.
entries.subject: Agentic AI orchestration
entries.note: Conditional prediction. Baseline market estimates cited: US$8.5 billion by 2026, US$35 billion by 2030.

entries.title: AI for industrial robotics, humanoid robots, and drones
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that the global cumulative installed capacity of industrial robots could reach 5.5 million by 2026, but annual new robot sales have stalled at just over half a million units since 2021.
entries.subject: Industrial robots and physical AI

entries.title: SaaS meets AI agents: Transforming budgets, customer experience, and workforce dynamics
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that up to half of organizations will put more than 50% of their digital transformation budgets toward AI automation in 2026
entries.metric: organizations putting >50% of digital transformation budgets into AI automation
entries.subject: AI agents in SaaS

entries.title: New technologies and familiar challenges could make semiconductor supply chains more fragile
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that in 2026, certain other advanced technologies and software tools that enable advanced AI models will become supply chain chokepoints.
entries.subject: Semiconductor supply chain

entries.title: Tiny episodes, massive appeal: Short-form serials are gaining viewers and empowering independent studios
entries.quote: In 2026, Deloitte predicts that the revenue growth of in-app micro-series will more than double, reaching $7.8 billion.
entries.subject: Micro-series (short-form serial video)

entries.title: Video podcasts dominate: Opportunity for brands, competition for traditional video
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that annual global podcast and vodcast advertising revenues will reach approximately $5 billion in 2026—a nearly 20% year-over-year rise.
entries.metric: global podcast and vodcast ad revenue
entries.subject: Video podcasts

entries.title: A new era of self-reliance: Navigating technology sovereignty
entries.quote: In 2026, Deloitte predicts that more countries will gain greater access to AI compute, and over US$100 billion will be committed to building sovereign AI compute.
entries.subject: Technology sovereignty

entries.title: Generative AI video is perfect for social media, but could disrupt social media companies
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that in 2026, generative video could provoke a regulatory response in the United States, potentially driving broader age verification in more states
entries.subject: Generative AI video

entries.title: Public media partnerships with streaming giants could be a model for making traditional TV sustainable
entries.quote: In 2026, Deloitte predicts another handful of broadcaster-and-streamer deals.
entries.subject: Public broadcaster and streamer partnerships

entries.title: Next-gen satellite internet is transforming pricing, capacity, and regulation worldwide
entries.quote: Deloitte also predicts that around 1,000 D2D satellites will provide low-bandwidth connectivity services (SOS, text, and voice) in areas that may lack terrestrial cell coverage
entries.subject: Direct-to-device satellite connectivity
entries.note: Same paragraph: D2D infrastructure spend expected at US$6-8 billion by 2026; Deloitte notes its 2024 figure of US$3 billion came in around US$4 billion.

entries.title: Gifts beat gigabits: Some mobile users rank rewards over network upgrades
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that in 2026, mobile operator reward schemes may matter to consumers in developed markets as much as—or even more than—network performance.
entries.subject: Mobile operator loyalty rewards

notes: 25th edition by count from 2002. Deloitte states 13 topics. Quotes from the edition overview page, except where the note names a chapter page. datePublished 2025-11-16 from page metadata.
